_comment: SQLite database-path resolution contract for Tina4 (ADR-0086).
The language-neutral answer key the four frameworks must agree on when they
turn a SQLite connection string into a path the driver opens. The four already
agreed on :memory: passthrough, unix-absolute passthrough, and relative-under-cwd;
they diverged on the mkdir mode, the escape guard, and the drive-letter path on a
POSIX host. This fixture pins all five cases; ADR-0086 says why.
Real resolver, real files, real mkdir in every framework - no mocks.
status: proven - one invariant, five cases, real per-language resolvers (no mocks)

schema.given: a SQLite connection string (or bare path) and the current working directory
schema.when: the shared resolver resolves it to a driver path
schema.then: the returned path, and whether a directory was created and with what mode
schema.error: a relative path whose parent escapes cwd raises the language's argument error

constants.escape_behaviour: refuse (raise), never a silent mkdir outside cwd and never a clamp

invariants.rule: One resolver, one answer per shape: :memory: and absolute (unix OR drive-letter, recognised on every OS) pass through with no mkdir; a relative path resolves under cwd and its parent is created with mode 0775 ONLY when it stays inside cwd; a relative path whose parent escapes cwd is REFUSED loudly, never a silent mkdir outside the project.

given.connection: an absolute /abs/missing/app.db whose parent does not exist

cases.name: drive letter absolute passthrough no mkdir
relative under cwd creates parent mode 0775

given.connection: sub/dir/app.db, cwd is the project root, umask 0

cases.name: relative escaping cwd is refused no mkdir

then.error: argument error naming the escaping path and the project root
